label: accepted

evidence.V1: Rectangular wall with a clear centred opening reads as a doorway in front, three-quarter and silhouette; door frame centred on the 8-stud width (front view ~255 of 256 px).
evidence.V2: Big wall mass, medium ashlar blocks / cap course / door frame, small gold keystone: three clear tiers.
evidence.V3: Proportions are plausible but very boxy: straight square-section frame, flat cap slab, and an unresolved dark recessed band between the frame lintel and the upper block course that reads as a gap rather than a designed lintel.
evidence.V4: Blocks, cap course and frame all carry consistent small chamfers that catch a highlight line in the studio close-ups.
evidence.V5: Doorway, lintel and end-section close-ups are clean: no z-fighting, pinches or stray faceting; geometry seams are designed block joints.
evidence.V6: One stone hue in three values (light, mid, dark blocks/threshold) plus the gold keystone accent; holds in sandstone and brick colourways.
evidence.V7: 540 tris vs module target 800 (ceiling 2000): under target.
evidence.V8: Single white vertex-colour material, chamfered made edges, stone hue + gold keystone per the modular kit; T1 tiling pass on the 2-stud grid.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, CollisionFidelity Default to keep the doorway walkable, CanTouch off, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic, grid-corner origin.

top_fixes: Resolve the dark recessed band above the door frame: fill it with a proper lintel stone or voussoir course so the opening reads designed
Give the door frame a little more shape (stepped architrave, slight arch or larger keystone) to lift it from plain square bars
Carry some block relief onto the end faces so the side view is not a flat slab when the wall ends exposed
